interrupt_controller.external: INT is internally synchronized and falling-edge latched. The retained latch has priority over the timer and clears when external-interrupt vector service begins.
interrupt_controller.timer: TIR remains pending while TIM or CCR I masks service. Software clears TIR; timer service does not clear it automatically.
interrupt_controller.response: After an unmasked hardware request is recognized, CPU-state stacking, I-bit setting, and vector fetching require 11 processor cycles. The documented bus sequence is two next-opcode-address reads; PCL, PCH, X, A, and CCR stack writes; an unused read at the decremented stack pointer; the selected high and low vector reads; and a trailing read at the address following the low vector byte. For an 11-bit PC, the five unused upper PCH bits stack as ones.
interrupt_controller.verification: All eight external-request, timer-request, and timer-mask combinations are checked independently in the model and directly in RTL. Real-core tests verify exact 11-cycle external and timer entry, every documented bus address/direction and stack byte, external priority and automatic latch clear, retained timer service, and both vector reads. The cycle-11 data input is explicitly non-comparable because the manufacturer labels it unusable; its address and read direction remain exact.

implementation_scope.firmware_storage: Address decode is internal; user EPROM, bootstrap ROM, and vector data use the FPGA firmware-memory port. Copyrighted bootstrap bytes are not redistributed.
implementation_scope.bootstrap: A separately qualified TIMER-pin high-voltage input selects the 7F6:7F7 vector when MOR secure mode is clear.
implementation_scope.programming: PCR PLE/PGE plus the digital VPP detector control EPROM read, address/data latch, and program-request outputs. User EPROM, MOR, and vector addresses are programmable; bootstrap ROM is not.
implementation_scope.ddr_read_discrepancy: The normalized boundary returns FF, following figures 4 and 16. Printed-page-13 prose instead classifies DDR reads as undefined, so silicon-equivalent read data remains UNDEFINED_BY_DOCUMENTATION.
implementation_scope.unspecified_port_latch_reset: The RTL selects deterministic zero for FPGA operation and makes no silicon-equivalence claim for the manufacturer-undefined reset value.
implementation_scope.unspecified_ram_reset: RAM is not reset because the manufacturer reset description does not define its initial contents.
analog_exclusions: EPROM programming voltage and pulse physics
